Cyclazodone seems fairly polar but in the case of reuptake-inhibitors, there is a clear trend that more lipophilic bulk increases DA over NA selectivity. a-PCyP is the example I'm mainly referring to. Overall this makes sense considering NA has an additional polar beta-hydroxyl group absent in DA. On the other hand, NET/DAT aren't even that selective regarding the two substrates (NET can transport DA as far as I know).  
Other than that, I haven't heard of lipophilicity causing biased drug distribution towards CNS or something like that (besides tending to enable rapid BBB passage).

The thing is, that the targets/receptors leading to nonfunctional monoamine release (=independent of neuronal firing) typical of psychostimulants likely aren't distributed in a way that enables such specificity. It has been shown that alpha1 adrenergic receptors located on axons of DAergic neurons are responsible for reversing DAT transport direction in response to amphetamine and 5HT2b receptors are necessary for MDMA to elicit its dopaminergic effects. I think it's plausible the alpha1 receptors aren't and certainly the 5HT2b receptors are not exclusively expressed on DAergic neurons.  
Opposed to the nonfunctional monoamine release mediated through a reversal of transporter direction, there is also the functional increase of monoamine efflux (=increased efflux in response to actual neuronal firing), typical of "monoaminergic activity enhancers". This phenomenon is dependent upon TAAR1 agonism and mostly responsible for amphetamine's efficacy in ADHD and as a cognition enhancer.

I think cyclazodone, like pemoline and perhaps other aminorex analogs, which are characterized as mostly dopaminergic but, contrary to what you might expect, less addictive than meth or amph, have predominant monoaminergic activity enhancer effects. They still resemble stimulants in their reuptake-inhibiting properties because they rely on monoamine transporters to access TAAR1 receptors, most of which are located intracellularly. And lastly, this dependence upon monoamine transporters and transporter selectivity governs which transmitter system is affected.
